title: the Range header cursor is advanced by a fixed skip past the end of its file-scope chunk and the parse reads on inside the same block
live_proof: absent at the 4.6.8 pin, read two-sided from the pinned tree: the vulnerable unconditional skips have ZERO occurrences in v4.6.8:epan/dissectors/packet-http.c (grep 'first_range_num_str += 6' and 'str += 8' both 0), while the fix's own RFC 9110 range-set commentary is present (3 occurrences of 'ranges-specifier'/'range-unit'), and the pin parses with bounds-aware ws_strtou64(pos, &pos, &first_range_num) at :3936 and :3955 instead of pointer skips. The pre-fix shape is quoted from 0261fd7da6^ at packet-http.c:3740-3745 (the '+= 6' site) and :3788-3790 (the '+= 8' site this case models).
object: the Range header value copied into file scope, 6 bytes for the value used here
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive for the whole case. This is the corpus's only spatial row: no lifetime ends, the cursor simply leaves the chunk. The field is required by the schema and is answered honestly rather than left to imply a reuse that does not happen.
shape: cursor advanced past its chunk by a fixed skip, read inside the same block
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. wmem_strdup is written as its own alloc+copy because the corpus seam includes wmem_core only; the skip is upstream's literal 8; the parse that follows is reduced to its first read, which is the byte the cursor lands on.
distinguishing: the corpus's first SPATIAL row, and the first upstream spatial defect reduced in this tree: no lifetime ends, the cursor leaves its 6-byte chunk inside the same block. Only a bound at the chunk can see it, so it separates the arm that bounds wmem's objects (virtual-nested-pools) from the ones that bound only what the system allocator hands out.
note: File scope, not the packet pool, which is why upstream's own defect is here: wmem_file_scope() is a BLOCK allocator. docs/ref/wireshark-spatial-defect-triage.md records the two LIVE spatial defects that sit in BLOCK_FAST.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-cheribsd-libc/: **NOT CAUGHT** on stock wmem with the system allocator as CheriBSD's libc (WM_LIBC_SYSTEM, WM_CHUNKS=OFF), revocation on: the crossing stayed inside one g_malloc'd block and completed; fixed arm VERDICT FIXED. In the same boot control 90 (a jumbo g_free'd by the reset) was HELD by the quarantine and the revocation control faulted at its labelled load. The 2026-10-07 reading of this arm ran the hosted bump arena with the chunk port compiled in, where nothing reached free().

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O0; wmem and the port built with the same flags). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 402653184` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 402653184` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (b64cd18b85d0); the arm was previously 'declined'.
native-detect.note: DECLINED, not pending, and the reason is a measurement rather than an estimate: the two-sided shape is already established by the FFmpeg sub-object probe (ffmpeg/subobject-repros/results/20261005-native-subobject/asan-probe.c), where the member-to-member crossing draws NO report while a write one element past the whole allocation draws heap-buffer-overflow. Every crossing in this corpus stays inside one g_malloc'd block or slab page by the same mechanism, so eight more silent-with-control runs would confirm what one already showed. Two further reasons not to spend them: the wireshark corpus has no standalone native build to instrument, and the memcached one would have to instrument the case while linking an uninstrumented port library -- the mixed mode in which that probe's own -O1 artefact arose, where BOTH arms went silent because the dead stores were optimised away. If this arm is ever wanted, it needs its positive control in the same binary.
native-detect.prediction: NO ASan report, and that is the finding rather than a gap: the overread stays inside the one g_malloc'd block, so there is no redzone between the chunks for ASan to poison. Needs its own positive control -- a read past the END of the block, which ASan must report -- or a silent arm proves nothing about the subject and something about the instrument.
native-detect.measured: 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-native-asan-libc/run-asan.txt: SILENT, the defect reproduced; wmem built with WM_LIBC_SYSTEM=ON (g_malloc/g_free are the host's malloc/free); wmem's own control 90 reported heap-use-after-free at wm_probe in the same run. The earlier reading (2026-10-09) ran the hosted bump arena, which could read nothing else.

native-fix-differential.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-differential/: the buggy sequence reaches storage outside its object (VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, exit 0) and the fixed sequence -- this case's upstream fix, modelled in case.c under wm_fixed -- does not (VERDICT FIXED, exit 0). Hosted build, upstream wmem allocator (WM_CHUNKS=OFF), `program 0 N buggy|fixed` (runners/run-native.sh). Spatial: the access address lies outside [object, object+size) in the buggy sequence and inside it, or is not made, in the fixed one. The arm did not exist before 2026-10-09: the cases had no fixed sequence.

nested_why: an inner allocator carved the crossed region out of a larger block it had itself obtained, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row IS NESTED.
